newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine opposition ahead in Congress polls.
newsitem.headline: Argentine opposition ahead in Congress polls.

text.p: Candidates for Argentina's center-left Frepaso alliance are ahead in the race for two key seats for October's partial congressional elections, according to a poll published Sunday.

In Buenos Aires province -- Argentina's biggest electoral district -- Frepaso's Graciela Fernandez Meijide is attracting 34.7 percent of support, according to private pollsters Graciela Romer y Asociados in the La Nacion newspaper.
Behind Fernandez Meijide was Hilda Gonzalez de Duhalde, of the governing Peronist Party, with 33.3 percent.

In the symbolically vital seat of the city of Buenos Aires, Frepaso's Carlos Alvarez led Rodolfo Terragno of the Radical Party by 27.3 percent to 25.1 percent. Peronist candidate Daniel Scioli was fifth with 4.2 percent, behind former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo -- now running an anti-corruption campaign -- with 10.4 percent.
La Nacion did not report when the survey was taken, how many people were interviewed, or the margin of error of the poll.
